**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, November 19, 2024, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present in addition to Mr. Schmidt: Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, and Wilson. Dr. Philippart was absent. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Pagel, Malutan, and Trudel. Approximately 140 members of the audience attended. The meeting adjourned at 9:43 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.

**Recognition / Mission Moment**
Hamilton Elementary School was recognized for its designation as a National Blue Ribbon School, honored at a ceremony in Washington, D.C. on November 7th and 8th by U.S. Secretary of Education Miguel Cardona. Only 356 schools nationwide were chosen for the honor in 2024.

The Communications Department was recognized for receiving 15 Michigan School and Public Relations Association (MSPRA) awards, the most the team has ever received: three awards of excellence and 12 awards of merit. Staff named: Melissa Verduyn, Thomas Butcher, Adam Burns, Linda Alfonso, Patrice Rowbal, and Alison Hendry. Awards were received in October, with recognition to follow at the MSPRA conference in March.

**Consent Agenda**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mr. Haupt, to approve items A, B, C, and D: minutes of the October 1, 2024 Board Workshop; minutes of the October 15, 2024 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report for September 2024; and rescheduling the January 7, 2025 Board Workshop to January 14, 2025. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Curriculum**
Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent of Elementary Instruction, and Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction, presented a student achievement data review covering summative and formative assessments and a county comparison of M-Step, PSAT, and SAT scores.

**Business**
Michael Walsh, Audit Partner from Plante Moran, presented highlights of the 2023-2024 fiscal year audit; a draft report had been presented in detail at the November 12, 2024 Board Workshop. Results included an unmodified opinion with no findings or questioned costs in the 2024 financial statement and the 2024 federal program audit, plus the ASBO Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for 2023. Finance Director Aurel Malutan and Assistant Superintendent Dan Trudel were recognized.

| Item | Vendor | Amount | Fund |
|---|---|---|---|
| Three UNOX ovens (Hill, Leonard, Troy Union) | Stafford Smith | $118,203.00 | Food Service Fund |
| New Smith Middle School landscape work | Heritage and Company, Inc. | $1,239,877.00 | Capital Projects Fund |
| 2025 roof replacement | (awarded as listed) | — | Capital Projects Fund |
| New servers and back-up software | People Driven Technology | $443,866.88 | Capital Projects Fund and General Fund |
| Two electric school buses | Hoekstra Transportation | $815,082.00 | 74b Clean Bus Energy Grant |

All business motions, including acceptance of the audited 2024 financial statements, passed Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

**Public Communication and Other**
No one spoke on agenda items. Thirteen community members addressed the Board during non-agenda public communication; no action was taken. Student representatives Diana D'Aloisio (Athens High School), Kristian Vitanovich (Troy College and Career High School), Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East), and Adam McManus (Troy High School) reported on school events. Board members congratulated Audra Melton, Ayesha Potts, and Stephanie Zendler on winning the election and thanked Mr. Hauff, Mr. Schmidt, and Dr. Wilson for their years of service. The next Board Workshop was announced for December 3rd at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building and the next regular meeting for December 17th at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building.
2024_144_m111924bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held November 19, 2024, at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, and Wilson were present; Dr. Philippart was absent. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators DiPilato, Griffor, Montante, Pagel, Malutan, and Trudel. Approximately 140 members of the audience were in attendance. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, and carry the notation GH/jh.

RECOGNITION / MISSION MOMENT — NATIONAL BLUE RIBBON AWARD, HAMILTON ELEMENTARY SCHOOL. The Board recognized Hamilton Elementary School for its designation as a National Blue-Ribbon School, an award honoring the school as one of the very best schools in the United States. Hamilton was recognized by U.S. Secretary of Education Miguel Cardona at a ceremony in Washington, D.C. on November 7th and 8th. Only 356 schools from around the country were chosen for this honor in 2024. The minutes note that the award affirms the hard work of students, staff, parents, and the Hamilton community, and quote Secretary Cardona's press release statement that "The National Blue Ribbon Schools Award is a testament to the exceptional achievements of students and educators at each of these schools," that the 2024 National Blue Ribbon Schools are "raising the bar for our nation's students, serving as models for effective teaching and intentional collaboration in their schools and communities," and calling on the country to look to these schools for inspiration "as we champion education as the foundation of a brighter future for every child."

RECOGNITION — 2024 MICHIGAN SCHOOL PUBLIC RELATIONS ASSOCIATION (MSPRA) AWARDS. The Board recognized the Troy School District Communications Department and invited team members forward. The Communications team received 15 Michigan School and Public Relations Association (MSPRA) awards, the most the team has ever received. Staff thanked by name were Melissa Verduyn, Thomas Butcher, Adam Burns, Linda Alfonso, Patrice Rowbal, and newest team member Alison Hendry. The department was recognized with three awards of excellence and 12 awards of merit.

Awards of Excellence were received in the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion category for "Elevating Voices: In Comfortably Uncomfortable Conversations" podcast; the Marketing Materials category for Early College with LTU; and the Special Purpose category for Coffee with the Superintendent.

Awards of Merit were received in the Marketing Materials category for the Career Accelerator Program; Marketing Materials for the College and Career Fair; Marketing Materials for the Summer School Catalog; Newsletter category for TSD News Supplement - Spring 2024 - Summer 2024; Special Purpose category for Board of Education Community Conversation; Special Purpose category for Smith Middle School Orchestra; Video category for "Why Flexible Seating"; Video category for "Danielle Clippard - Outstanding Support Staff 2024"; Video category for "Autism Acceptance: Morse Friendship Cookies"; Video category for "Beyond: Flying Drones with Jack Kelly"; Video category for "Celebrating Manufacturing Day"; and Audio/Podcast category for "Inside TSD with Dr. Rich Machesky - June 2024." The team received the awards in October and will be recognized at the MSPRA conference in March. The minutes record the district's pride in the department's creative talent and its dedication to sharing the stories and successes of the Troy School District and to "world-class excellence."

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS: None. PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS): None.

GENERAL — CONSENT AGENDA. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, and D on the consent agenda: minutes of the October 1, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the October 15, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; the Treasurer's Report for September 2024; and rescheduling the January 7, 2025 Board Workshop to January 14, 2025. The vote was Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

PERSONNEL: None.

CURRICULUM — STUDENT ACHIEVEMENT DATA REVIEW. Kris Griffor, Assistant Superintendent of Elementary Instruction, and Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction, shared a report updating the Board on student achievement data. They explained how the data is used to drive the district's systems and processes, discussed summative and formative assessments, and reviewed county comparisons of M-Step, PSAT, and SAT scores.

BUSINESS — 2023/2024 AUDIT REPORT. Mr. Michael Walsh, Audit Partner from Plante Moran, presented to the Board of Education on the audit of the 2023-2024 fiscal year. A draft copy of the District's Audit Report had been presented in detail to the Board at the November 12, 2024 Board of Education Workshop. Mr. Walsh provided highlights and reported an unmodified opinion with no findings or questioned costs in the 2024 financial statement and in the 2024 federal program audit results, and mentioned the ASBO Certificate of Excellence in Financial Reporting for 2023. Governmental funds, revenue and expenditures were reviewed, along with student population, foundation allowance, and changes in federal funding. The audit partners and Board members recognized the Business Services team, Finance Director Aurel Malutan and Assistant Superintendent Dan Trudel, for their work managing the budget.

2023/2024 AUDIT — ACTION. It was moved by Mr. Haupt and supported by Mr. Hauff that the Board of Education accept and approve the Troy School District's audited 2024 financial statements as presented by Plante Moran. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

OVEN REPLACEMENT FOR HILL, LEONARD, AND TROY UNION. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the purchase of three UNOX ovens be awarded to Stafford Smith in the amount of $118,203.00, approved as an expenditure of the Food Service Fund. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

NEW SMITH MIDDLE SCHOOL — LANDSCAPE CATEGORY. It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mr. Hauff that the bid for landscape work at the new Smith Middle School be awarded to Heritage and Company, Inc. in the amount of $1,239,877.00, approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

2025 ROOF REPLACEMENT PROJECT. It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Alic that the bid for roof replacement be awarded as set out in the resolution and that the amount be approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund. The award detail appears in a table that is not captured in the extracted text of these minutes. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

INFRASTRUCTURE UPGRADES. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Alic that the contract for new servers and back-up software be awarded to People Driven Technology in the amount of $443,866.88, approved as an expenditure of the Capital Projects Fund and General Fund. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

ELECTRIC BUSSES PURCHASE. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Mrs. Anne that the bid for two electric school buses be awarded to Hoekstra Transportation in the amount of $815,082.00, approved as an expenditure of the 74b Clean Bus Energy Grant. Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Thirteen community members addressed the Board during public communication. No action was taken by the Board.

OTHER: None.

REPORTS FROM HIGH SCHOOL STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES. Diana D'Aloisio, student representative for Athens High School, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Kristian Vitanovich, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, shared a report on his school. Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, shared a report on her school. Adam McManus, student representative for Troy High School, shared a report on his school.

BOARD COMMENTS. Board members shared upcoming events of possible community interest and congratulated Audra Melton, Ayesha Potts, and Stephanie Zendler for winning the election. They shared sentiments and thanked Mr. Hauff, Mr. Schmidt, and Dr. Wilson for their dedication and years of service as Board members to Troy School District students and the community. Mr. Schmidt announced that he would not be in attendance for the December workshop or meeting and shared sentiments about his years of service on the Troy Board of Education. He announced that the next Board Workshop would be held in the Administration Building on December 3rd at 6:00 p.m., and the next regular meeting on December 17th in the Services Building at 7:00 p.m.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting adjourned at 9:43 p.m.
